problem: Existing Expertise Packs cover generic product hierarchy, responsive interaction, and accessibility, but they do not decide why motion exists, which elements should use triggered versus progress-linked behavior, how scroll storytelling and microinteractions should be orchestrated, or how their UX impact, motion safety, and runtime performance should be verified.
reusable_when: Designing or implementing scroll-triggered reveals and scroll-linked storytelling
Designing motion systems, page transitions, and component microinteractions
Reviewing interactive web motion for UX impact, accessibility, and performance
Choosing between native CSS, Web APIs, and animation libraries for a bounded effect
not_for: Generic web layout, typography, visual hierarchy, or responsive composition without a motion decision
Video playback, game animation, canvas rendering, or 3D scene engineering as the primary decision family
Brand-only moodboards or visual styling without interactive behavior
Generic release QA or browser testing strategy already owned by software-qa
existing_coverage: product-design owns screen briefs, typography, visual hierarchy, generic interaction states, responsive layout, accessibility, and reference selection. It does not own motion purpose, scroll-trigger mechanics, scroll-linked narrative behavior, choreography, motion-specific accessibility controls, or animation runtime evidence.

proposed_guides.failure_prevented: Decorative motion consumes attention, delays tasks, or creates disorientation without a named user need or measurable benefit.
decision_checks: Name the motion's job: feedback, continuity, orientation, hierarchy, progressive disclosure, or deliberate emphasis
Map the effect to a specific element, user moment, and expected behavior change
Compare a static or lower-motion alternative before accepting the attention and performance cost
Define task, error, orientation, comfort, and runtime evidence that can confirm or reject the hypothesis

proposed_guides.failure_prevented: Independent animations use inconsistent duration, easing, distance, and sequencing, making the interface feel noisy and obscuring hierarchy or state.
decision_checks: Define a small token set for duration, easing, distance, stagger, and reduced motion
Separate frequent productive motion from rare expressive motion
Coordinate related elements by hierarchy and causal order rather than animating every child independently
Define interruption, reversal, re-entry, exit, and route-change cleanup behavior

proposed_guides.failure_prevented: Viewport-entry reveals hide important content, replay unexpectedly, break reading order, or fail when JavaScript, observation, or hydration is unavailable.
decision_checks: Use a triggered reveal only when entry timing adds hierarchy or orientation beyond ordinary document flow
Define observation threshold, root margin, once-or-repeat behavior, and group stagger
Keep semantic order and critical content available before enhancement succeeds
Verify fast scrolling, reverse scrolling, resize, deep links, hydration, and reduced-motion fallback

proposed_guides.failure_prevented: Scrub, pin, parallax, snap, or horizontal scenes hijack scrolling, trap content, separate narration from visuals, or collapse on small screens.
decision_checks: Use progress-linked motion only when scroll position meaningfully represents narrative or spatial progress
Define scene boundaries, pin duration, progress mapping, focus order, escape path, and content continuity
Choose native scroll timelines or a library from required capability, support, fallback, and lifecycle evidence
Verify keyboard, touch, trackpad, reverse scroll, short viewport, zoom, reduced motion, and unsupported-browser behavior

proposed_guides.failure_prevented: Hover-only or gesture-only microinteractions produce inconsistent feedback across mouse, touch, keyboard, and assistive input or display a state that differs from application truth.
decision_checks: Map hover, focus, press, drag, loading, success, error, disabled, and selected motion to authoritative component state
Match feedback strength and latency to the significance and reversibility of the action
Provide equivalent cues and activation paths for every supported input modality
Verify interruption, rapid repetition, focus movement, pointer cancellation, and async state replacement

proposed_guides.failure_prevented: Interaction motion causes vestibular discomfort, distraction, flashing risk, or inaccessible drag and continuous-animation behavior.
decision_checks: Classify essential and non-essential motion and provide a useful reduced or static alternative
Honor prefers-reduced-motion and add explicit pause, stop, hide, or frequency controls where required
Keep flashing within WCAG thresholds and avoid large peripheral, zooming, or parallax movement by default
Give drag interactions a non-drag pointer alternative and preserve keyboard, focus, semantics, and information

proposed_guides.failure_prevented: Animation appears correct in code review but drops frames, triggers layout or paint, leaks observers or timelines, or degrades input responsiveness in the real page.
decision_checks: Choose CSS, native Web APIs, or a library by required orchestration rather than habit
Prefer transform and opacity when they express the effect and isolate unavoidable layout or paint work
Scope observers and animation instances, batch reads and writes, refresh geometry deliberately, and clean up on route or component teardown
Record representative runtime traces and rendered behavior across viewport, device, input, and reduced-motion conditions

pass_criteria: Interactive motion requests select the candidate and no more than four directly relevant Guides
Scroll-triggered and scroll-linked behavior remain distinct decisions
Every motion recommendation includes purpose, fallback, motion-safety, and runtime evidence appropriate to its scope
Compatibility-sensitive browser or library requests open contextual research
regression_criteria: Generic layout, typography, and visual-only work remains routed to product-design
Backend, video-provider, game, canvas, and 3D implementation are not selected from generic motion words
The Pack never grants repository or external write authority
Library capability is never treated as proof that an effect benefits UX
